messages:
maria: FYI found a permissions issue during a canary rollback attempt. Non-admin user could trigger rollback from Console. :warning:

samir: can you paste steps and which user/role? do we have an exploit or just UI showing the button? :eyes:

maria: repro on staging with role 'release-engineer' (should only be able to view canaries). Steps: login as release-engineer -> Console -> Canary detail -> click 'Rollback' -> confirm -> rollback started. No 403 returned.

jen: ouch. that sounds like server-side check missing. UI-only gating would explain it. did the API return 202 or 200?

maria: API returned 202 and triggered rollout service. I pulled logs: deploy service called by user id 1029, auth header present. No RBAC denial in the logs.

deploy-bot: [automated] rollout.request id=rl-2026-03-20-92 user=1029 target=canary-23 status=accepted

samir: timeline: when did we last touch RBAC for rollouts? I think the 'rollouts' permission split landed in the refactor last month. Maybe mapping lost 'rollback' action.

tom: @samir correct — we refactored roles last sprint. In ACLs we moved from granular string actions to verbs, and I remember a mismatch on the server check. I can inspect service auth layer.

alisa: can you grep for checks around 'rollout:rollback' vs 'rollout:modify'? my hunch: client sent 'rollback' but server checks for 'modify' or vice versa.

pete: adding audit/KMS angle: KMS logs show the rollback request was signed with customer KMS key (ok), but CloudAudit shows no 'permission:rollback' denied events — meaning the decision never hit IAM.

samir: please run quick audit query: list recent rollout actions where user role != admin and action in (rollback, abort). we need blast radius.

maria: ran query on staging timeframe: 5 rollbacks by release-engineer in last 3 hours, 0 aborts. none should have succeeded.

jen: mitigations: 1) temporary disable rollback button via feature-flag 2) add server-side guard returning 403 if caller lacks explicit 'rollout.rollback' permission 3) rollback any unintended rollouts (manual intervention)

samir: agreed. I'll open a patch. quick patch idea (server):

```
// auth check pseudocode
if (!authz.hasPermission(caller, "rollout.rollback")) {
  return 403
}
```

tom: working on a minimal PR to enforce exact permission. Will also add a unit test covers UI+API path.

alisa: also add audit log entry schema: include granted_permissions snapshot at time of action and KMS key id. helps investigations.

pete: creating an incident ticket and tagging compliance. Need to know if any customer data was exposed; looks like just control plane action but we should notify any customers with config-protected rollouts.

maria: status: feature-flag toggled off for rollback button in prod console (disabled). Tom's PR targeting hotfix branch, will push once CI green.

deploy-bot: [automated] ci.build rl-auth-check #142 passed in 2m 18s

tom: PR merged to hotfix, deploying to canary infra now. patch enforces server-side check for 'rollout.rollback' and logs permission set.

samir: after deploy, run smoke: attempt rollback as release-engineer on staging, should get 403 and UI show disabled/tooltip.

maria: smoke on staging now returns 403. UI shows tooltip "insufficient permissions". :lock:

jen: next steps: 1) backfill audit logs for last 24h with decision=false where appropriate 2) prepare customer notification template for impacted orgs 3) postmortem and add RBAC regression test to e2e suite

pete: compliance: include KMS audit context in the notification. I'll draft message and list affected customer IDs.

samir: good work. assign owners: tom (hotfix + e2e test), alisa (audit log schema + query), pete (incident ticket + customer notice), jen (postmortem & retro). keep updates in this thread.

maria: adding notes to incident runbook, saving logs to secure bucket (kms-encrypted).

tom: deploy to prod complete. monitoring for anomalies.

maria: closing loop: prod verification shows 403 for non-admins. will reopen if anything else shows up. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
